reasoning: The January 2024 meeting removes the 'additional policy firming' language and replaces it with 'considering any adjustments to the target range,' and explicitly states the Committee 'does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.' This is a language refinement that formalizes what was already signaled in December 2023 — that the peak rate had likely been reached — rather than a transition between regimes. The rate target is unchanged at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent, QT continues on the same schedule, and no actual easing has begun; the Committee is still in a holding/pause regime established at the prior meeting.
key_quote: the Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent
